utils/slab_data.py:75 hard-codes base_dir '/home/t-dimaha/RobustDG/robustdg/data/datasets/slab/'. data_gen_syn.py writes to relative 'data/datasets/slab/', so this path must be changed.

--slab_noise 0.1 in reproduce_slab.py is corruption of the slab-7 feature (corrupt_slab7), applied identically to every domain. The domains differ only in the linear-component corruption (spur_corr = domain name). The caption's 'noise 0.0/0.1/1.0' is the linear-component corruption.

Data are regenerated per run: the pickle seed equals the run index, generated with np.random.seed(seed*10). Each pickle holds 10000 points. The loader takes the first --slab_num_samples (default 1000) points. Train = 1000 per domain, val = 250 per domain (base_size/4), test = 1000 per domain. Val uses the source domains, 0.0 and 0.10, so no target data is used for validation.

train.py prints two numbers. 'Source Validation' is the test accuracy at the epoch with the highest source-val accuracy. 'Target Validation' is np.max over epochs of the test-domain accuracy, an oracle choice that reads the target domain. np.std is the population SD. Which one the paper table reports cannot be determined from the code. The 'evaluate' case of reproduce_slab.py runs test.py per_domain_acc with --acc_data_case train, which gives source-domain accuracy (Source 1 and Source 2 columns) using the saved best-val checkpoint. It does not give the target column.

The checkpoint is saved whenever val acc strictly exceeds the best so far (max_val_acc starts at 0.0). The best epoch is also reported as the max over 100 epochs. Test and val accuracy are computed every epoch.

Optimizer in BaseAlgo.get_opt: SGD with momentum=0.9 and nesterov=True hard-coded, lr 0.1 from the command, weight_decay default 5e-4 because the script does not pass it. A StepLR(step_size=25) scheduler is created in BaseAlgo.__init__ but scheduler.step() is never called, so lr is constant. ErmMatch only rebuilds the optimizer for lenet/domain_bed_mnist, not slab.

DANN and CDANN (algorithms/dann.py) do not use BaseAlgo's optimizer. They use two plain SGD optimizers (discriminator+class embedding; featurizer+classifier) with lr 0.01, no momentum and weight_decay 5e-4, ignoring --lr 0.1. Discriminator and generator updates alternate per epoch, not per batch: epoch % (1+d_steps) < d_steps updates the discriminator only. DANN: lambda 0.01, grad_penalty 0.1, d_steps 4. CDANN: grad_penalty 1.0, d_steps 2, with a class embedding added to the features. The generator loss is CE - lambda*disc_loss. The weight is constant.

MMD, CORAL, C-MMD and C-CORAL all use method_name mmd with penalty_ws 0.1, a constant weight. The penalty is on the 100-d post-ReLU feat_net features. MMD uses a Gaussian multi-bandwidth kernel; CORAL uses the mean+covariance difference ('mean_cov'). The conditional variants compute the penalty per class. The loss is CE on the plain batch of 128 (the batch mixes both source domains) plus gamma*mmd.

ERM, RandMatch and PerfMatch all use algorithms/erm_match.py. Training uses matched batches only (128 matched tuples, so 256 samples, one per domain). CE is computed on the matched samples. The matching penalty is the squared-L2 distance between logits (match_layer logit_match, pos_metric l2) across the two domains, with weight penalty_ws*(epoch - penalty_s)/(epochs - penalty_s) = penalty_ws*(epoch+1)/101, since penalty_s=-1 and match_flag=0. This is a linear ramp, and it is zero for ERM (penalty_ws 0.0). ERM in this repo is therefore 'erm_match' with random matching and no penalty. RandMatch has match_case 0.0 and penalty_ws 1.0. PerfMatch has match_case 1.0 and penalty_ws 1.0.
The model SlabClf is: Linear(2,100)+ReLU as the featurizer, then Linear(100,100) followed directly by Linear(100,2), with no nonlinearity between the last two.

Seeds: n_runs=10. In each run random, numpy and torch are seeded with run*10. Run r also uses data pickle seed r. There is no hyperparameter tuning in the repo for the paper's table (slab-tune.py exists but is not part of reproduce_slab.py). Hyperparameters such as penalty_ws and the DANN settings are hard-coded in reproduce_slab.py.

The slab-run.py script, which uses methods erm/irm/csd/rand/matchdg/perf, 3 seeds and test domains 0.9, is a different experiment. Its slab_noise comes from the command line (default 0.0) and it does not include MMD, CORAL or DANN. The reproduce_slab.py train case is the one that covers the Table 1 methods.
DANN uses the model's 'disc' head, which is declared in SlabClf. The train accuracy that DANN logs is computed after the update.

Which one the paper reports is not determined by the code. Both come with np.std (population SD) over 3 runs.
The script passes --dataset, but train.py defines --dataset_name; argparse prefix abbreviation resolves it. Default dataset_name is already rot_mnist.

Sample counts assume the notebook's --subset_size 1000 (script default is 2000): 1000 train and 200 val images per domain. Test data for domain d reuses the same base images as train (res[:subset_size]), only rotated differently, for the same seed.
Seeds 0,1,2 pick different base MNIST subsets (data_gen seed*10), and run index = mnist_subset in the loader. Training seeds are run*10.

ERM, RandMatch and PerfMatch share the same code (erm_match). The CE loss is computed only on the matched batch (all domains' matched points); the raw batch x_e is not used in the loss. ERM uses penalty_ws=0 with random matches.
In erm_match, penalty_ws ramps as penalty_ws*(epoch+1)/(epochs+1), since penalty_s=-1 and match_flag=0. Penalty distance is l2 on logits (pos_metric default l2, match_layer logit_match).

MatchDG phase 2 (matchdg_erm): loss = CE on matched points + CE on the plain batch + ramp*penalty_ws*l2 logit matching, ramp=(epoch+1)/(epochs+1). Matches are inferred from the phase-1 contrastive model (match_case -1, 100 matches per point); match_flag defaults to 0, so matches are not refreshed.

MatchDG phase 1 trains with only the NT-Xent style contrastive loss (weight ramp (epoch+1)/51), no CE; matches are refreshed every 5 epochs (match_interrupt default 5) with match_flag 1; the checkpoint is chosen every 5 epochs by top-10 perfect-match score on the val data of the source domains, using both augmented and original copies (match_func_aug_case 1). No lr schedule applies in phase 1 (the StepLR scheduler in BaseAlgo is created but never stepped).

The stored augmented copy (RandomResizedCrop scale 0.7-1 plus horizontal flip, applied after rotation) is only read in MatchDG phase 1 for checkpoint selection. All training and evaluation otherwise use the *_org_data.pt files because mnist_aug defaults to 0.

The LR schedule in phase 2 / erm_match for lenet rebuilds SGD at epochs 25, 50, 75 with lr=0.01/2^k, which also resets momentum buffers. The optimizer is SGD momentum 0.9 with nesterov True hard-coded (the --opt flag only switches to Adam).
Test data for lenet uses mnist_subset=run (same as train), not seed 9. 90-degree data is not generated for lenet.
No hyperparameter tuning scripts for this experiment; hyperparameters are fixed in the reproduce script and argparse defaults.

The data are one random draw (np.random.choice, with replacement) of subset_size+val_size indices per seed in [0,1,2]. Train and test both use res[:subset_size]. So for the lenet case the test domain is the same 1000 base digits as the training domains, rotated by the test angle. Validation uses res[subset_size:], also with replacement.
In the lenet case train.py reads test data with seed=`run`, not 9, because of `args.mnist_case not in ['lenet']`.

Seeds: n_runs=3 (default), seeds run*10 = 0, 10, 20. The data subset index is also `run` (0,1,2), so each run uses a different data draw. matchdg_erm runs n_runs_matchdg_erm=1 inner run per outer run.

Reported number: train.py prints two lines per test domain, np.mean and np.std (population SD, ddof=0) over the 3 runs. 'Final Test Accuracy (Source Validation)' takes the test accuracy at the epoch with the best source-validation accuracy. 'Final Test Accuracy (Target Validation)' takes the max over epochs of test accuracy on the target domain, which is oracle selection. The code does not say which line goes into the table. The per-domain files in results/rmnist_lenet/ hold both. The 'Average' column over the 6 test domains is not computed anywhere in these scripts.

All methods except matchdg_ctr use `erm_match`/`matchdg_erm` training on matched batches. Each step draws, for each of 16 base points, one random match from every training domain. The batch is 16 x 5 = 80 images and the cross-entropy is computed on those images. ERM therefore trains on random-matched (class-matched) batches with ws weight 0, not on plain shuffled batches. Matching is class-aware, base domain per class is the domain with the most samples.

RandMatch uses match_case 0.0, so perm_prob=1 and every match is random within the class, with total_matches_per_point=100 (one is chosen at random per step via random.choice). PerfMatch uses match_case 1.0 and perfect_match=1, so it matches the same object index in every domain. ERM uses match_case 0.0 with total_matches_per_point=1, and ws weight 0. match_flag defaults to 0, so matches are never re-inferred in these methods.

MatchDG phase 2 (matchdg_erm) uses match_case -1, so the initial matches are inferred with the phase-1 LeNet features (l2 distance on the 10-d logits, fc_layer is not used by lenet), top 100 matches per point. It uses pos_metric l2 (default, not cos). Matches are not refreshed because match_flag=0. The loss is cross-entropy on the matched batch + cross-entropy on an extra plain batch (erm_loss_extra, a standard shuffled batch of 16) + ramped ws penalty. The phase-1 checkpoint loaded is Model_<ctr_match_case>_<ctr_match_interrupt>_<ctr_match_flag>_<run>_lenet.pth from results/rot_mnist/matchdg_ctr/logit_match/train_<domains>/.

MatchDG phase 1 (matchdg_ctr): 50 epochs, batch 512, SGD lr 0.01 constant (BaseAlgo builds a StepLR scheduler but it is never stepped, and the lenet halving code only exists in the erm phases). Matches are random at epoch 0 and re-inferred every match_interrupt=5 epochs (match_flag 1). The loss is the NT-Xent-style diff_hinge_loss with tau 0.05 and cosine metric, weighted by (epoch+1)/51. Every 5 epochs it computes the top-10 perfect-match score on the source validation set, using the augmented and original copies of each validation image (match_func_aug_case=1), and saves the best. No accuracy is reported in this phase.

Learning rate for the erm phases: initial SGD(lr=0.01, momentum 0.9, nesterov, wd 5e-4). At epochs 25, 50, 75 a fresh SGD optimizer is built (momentum buffer reset) with lr = 0.01/2^(epoch//25), i.e. 0.005, 0.0025, 0.00125. This halving code is in the erm_match and match_dg erm phase and applies to lenet. The --opt flag is the default sgd and --lr is the default 0.01. The scripts pass neither.

Penalty ramp: weight = penalty_ws*(epoch - penalty_s)/(epochs - penalty_s) with penalty_s=-1, i.e. penalty_ws*(epoch+1)/101 for erm_match and matchdg_erm (100 epochs). The match_flag branch with match_interrupt does not apply, since match_flag=0 here.

The stored augmented copy (RandomResizedCrop(32, scale 0.7-1.0) + RandomHorizontalFlip applied after rotation, then ToTensor + Normalize) is saved as *_data.pt for train and val. Training reads it only if --mnist_aug 1, default 0, so it is not used for training in any method. Its one use here is the MatchDG phase-1 validation loader (MnistRotatedAugEval). Test images are never augmented. Because the loaders are called with mnist_aug=0, train/val/test for the erm phases use the *_org_data.pt files.
